A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EcoDiff in Learnable Sparsity for Vision Generative Models. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–J support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original pruning, retraining, ablation, and computational-cost results for SDXL, FLUX, and SD2 in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons in Table 1 and retraining experiments in Tables 2 and 10.

M1.justification: Sections 5.1–5.5 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same end-to-end objective, hard-concrete neuron masking, timestep gradient checkpointing, and optional LoRA or full-model retraining.

E1.justification: Both versions retain GCC3M-based calibration and synthetic retraining, LAION-subset retraining, and MS COCO/Flickr30K evaluation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains BK-SDM for SDXL, DiffPruning and Per-Step Loss for SDXL/FLUX, and FLUX-Lite for FLUX-Dev. Comparator membership in the appendix experiments also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6.1, Appendix B, and Tables 3, 4, and 7 retain the same sample sizes, metrics, preprocessing, budgets, and training configurations, including evaluation on 5,000 samples from each benchmark.

E4.justification: The pruning-ratio, regularization, calibration-size, module-selection, global/local thresholding, retraining-data, and compatibility analyses are retained. The complexity and carbon-footprint assessments are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 15 retains the statement that measurements are averaged over five runs. Neither the repeated-run information nor other statistical and uncertainty reporting changes.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative examples match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains EcoDiff SDXL FID values of 32.19 on MS COCO and 40.91 on Flickr30K.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, complexity reasoning in Section 5.4, and hard-concrete regularization derivation in Appendix A are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about efficient structural pruning, reduced optimization memory, and compatibility across architectures and acceleration methods.

C2.justification: Interpretations of semantic fidelity, degradation at higher sparsity, LoRA limitations, and architecture-dependent regularization remain unchanged. The shortened ethics paragraph restates the existing accessibility, environmental, and misuse discussion.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training information, and repository access remain unchanged. The reproducibility statement now explicitly points to Appendix B, which already contained the details in v2.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The references reflow across pages, and the Black Forest Labs access date changes format without changing the date.

P1.justification: v3 adds funding acknowledgments, separates the existing LLM disclosure under its own heading, shortens the ethics statement, and specifies Appendix B. It also updates publication and affiliation text and extends equal-contribution credit to Wenzhong Liang.

P2.justification: v3 changes the running header, compacts the affiliation block, and slightly shifts Figure 1 and the abstract. Closing statements and references reflow, with references starting on page 11 instead of page 10; scientific displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 adds acknowledgments and makes limited editorial and layout refinements. The methods, derivations, empirical evidence, substantive interpretations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
